assessed_and_not_taken.finding: The exact autosub contribution is a sum over the joint appearance states of ten outfield starters and three outfield substitutes — 8192 states — where which substitutes activate depends on which starters blanked and on formation legality after the swap. It is not a linear function of the selection variables and linearising it would need a variable per state per Gameweek.
assessed_and_not_taken.route: an exact reserve term in the solver objective
assessed_and_not_taken.verdict: Not possible without a major optimiser rewrite.

assessed_and_not_taken.finding: Enumerating legal elevens for a fixed fifteen is cheap — a few hundred — but the exact weekly score for each one still costs a joint-state integration, and the outer problem is choosing the fifteen from hundreds of players, not the eleven from fifteen.
assessed_and_not_taken.route: precomputed legal lineup and bench configurations
assessed_and_not_taken.verdict: Useful only after selection, which is where it is already used.

assessed_and_not_taken.finding: A Dantzig-Wolfe or branch-and-price formulation with squads as columns and the exact value as the column cost would price the right objective. The pricing subproblem is the nonlinear part and would need its own approximation, and the whole thing replaces the optimiser.
assessed_and_not_taken.verdict: Recorded as later work. It is the principled fix and it is out of scope here.

implemented.effect: It is the family that finds the exact winner on the live 2026/27 candidate set.
implemented.route: tighter linear surrogate, used for generation only
implemented.scope: Generation only. It never enters the exact decision value and cannot affect a ranking.
implemented.what: Reserve quality — every squad member's expected points in the Gameweeks they do not start — maximised inside a declared slack band on the primary objective.
implemented.why: It is the linear quantity most closely correlated with the autosub value the primary objective omits, and it is already built for the existing bench tie-break, so nothing new had to be modelled.

feasibility_assessment.note: Until one of those lands, the search is a generate-and-score procedure and no solver proof covers the exact objective. Nothing in this module claims global nonlinear optimality.

convergence.note: Balanced staged convergence: each stage expands every candidate family and the final stage is the whole pool, so the winning squad is always inside the last stage. Practical convergence only — no claim of global nonlinear optimality is made or implied: the exact objective is not the one the solver optimises, so no solver proof covers it.
